01-01.s: German neurologist Hermann Oppenheim was born; he later described the Oppenheim reflex and Oppenheim disease, advancing clinical neurological examination.
Swiss pediatrician Guido Fanconi was born; he went on to describe Fanconi anemia in 1927 and made foundational contributions to pediatric hematology and nephrology.

01-02.t: Sir Charles Bell Demonstrates Facial Nerve Palsy
01-02.s: Scottish anatomist and surgeon Sir Charles Bell publicly demonstrated his first classic case of facial nerve palsy, later known as Bell's palsy, before students at Middlesex Hospital.

01-02.t: Christiaan Barnard Performs Second Human Heart Transplant
01-02.s: South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed his second human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital on patient Philip Blaiberg, who survived for 593 days and helped prove long-term viability.

01-03.t: Foundation of the March of Dimes
01-03.s: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt established the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis, later known as the March of Dimes, to fund polio research and patient care.

01-03.t: First Bionic Hand with Sense of Touch Unveiled Outside a Lab
01-03.s: Researchers in Rome unveiled the first bionic hand equipped with sensory feedback capable of being used outside a laboratory setting, marking a milestone in neuroprosthetics.

01-04.t: Death of American Neurologist Silas Weir Mitchell
01-04.s: American physician Silas Weir Mitchell, who first described causalgia (complex regional pain syndrome), phantom limb pain, and erythromelalgia, died on this day.
The United Nations observed World Braille Day to celebrate the birth of Louis Braille and promote accessible communication and health literacy for people with visual impairments.

01-05.t: Public Announcement of Wilhelm Röntgen's Discovery of X-Rays
01-05.s: The Vienna newspaper Die Presse published a front-page report announcing Wilhelm Röntgen's discovery of X-rays, sparking immediate global excitement for medical imaging.

01-05.t: First Clinical Examination of Kawasaki Disease
01-05.s: Japanese pediatrician Tomisaku Kawasaki examined a four-year-old boy presenting with a distinctive febrile vasculitis syndrome, marking the first clinical recognition of Kawasaki disease.

01-06.t: Birth of English Surgeon Sir Percivall Pott
01-06.s: English surgeon Sir Percivall Pott was born; he later described Pott fracture, Pott disease (spinal tuberculosis), and identified chimney sweep's carcinoma as an occupational cancer.

01-06.t: First Adult Human Heart Transplant in the United States
01-06.s: Cardiothoracic surgeon Norman E. Shumway performed the first adult human-to-human heart transplant in the United States at Stanford University School of Medicine.

01-07.s: Slovakian-born American cardiologist William Ganz was born; he co-developed the Swan-Ganz pulmonary artery catheter in 1970 and pioneered early reperfusion therapy for myocardial infarction.

01-07.t: First Genetically Modified Pig Heart Transplanted into a Human
01-07.s: Surgeons at the University of Maryland Medical Center performed the first successful transplant of a genetically modified pig heart into a human patient, advancing xenotransplantation.

01-08.s: American psychologist Carl Rogers was born; he founded client-centered therapy, transforming modern psychotherapy and counseling practice.

01-08.t: Death of Cardiothoracic Surgeon Norman Rupert Barrett
01-08.s: Australian-born British surgeon Norman Barrett died; he is eponymously remembered for describing Barrett's esophagus and pioneering thoracic surgical techniques.

01-09.s: Japanese physician Hakaru Hashimoto died; in 1912 he published the first description of autoimmune chronic thyroiditis, now known as Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
American house painter Albert Stevens died after surviving more than two decades following an involuntary Manhattan Project plutonium injection, accumulating the highest known human radiation dose.

01-10.s: German physician and pathologist Karl Albert Ludwig Aschoff was born; he co-described the atrioventricular (Aschoff-Tawara) node and Aschoff bodies in rheumatic heart disease.
Surgeon Ivor Lewis delivered his Hunterian Lecture at the Royal College of Surgeons of England, introducing the two-stage surgical approach for esophageal carcinoma known as the Ivor Lewis procedure.

01-11.s: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson received the first human injection of insulin at Toronto General Hospital, marking a turning point that transformed Type 1 diabetes from a fatal diagnosis into a treatable condition.

01-11.t: First U.S. Surgeon General Report on Smoking and Health
01-11.s: U.S. Surgeon General Luther Terry released the landmark federal report warning that cigarette smoking is a major health hazard and cause of lung cancer.

01-12.t: First Use of Ether Anesthesia in France
01-12.s: French surgeon Joseph François Malgaigne presented his first clinical trials of ether anesthesia to the Académie de Médecine, accelerating its adoption across France.

01-12.t: First Continuous Epidural Catheter Analgesia in Childbirth
01-12.s: Romanian obstetrician Eugen Bogdan Aburel presented the first description of continuous epidural catheter analgesia for labor pain.

01-13.t: First Lumbar Epidural Catheter Technique Reported
01-13.s: In Havana, Manuel Martínez Curbelo reported the first lumbar epidural catheter technique for continuous segmental anesthesia using a ureteral catheter threaded through a Tuohy needle.

01-13.t: First Confirmed COVID-19 Case Outside China
01-13.s: Thailand's Ministry of Public Health reported the first laboratory-confirmed case of novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) outside China in a traveler from Wuhan.

01-14.t: First Recorded Successful Cesarean Section in the United States
01-14.s: Physician Jesse Bennett performed the first recorded successful cesarean section in the United States on his wife, Elizabeth Bennett, with both mother and infant surviving.

01-15.t: Birth of Surgeon François Gigot de La Peyronie
01-15.s: French surgeon François Gigot de La Peyronie was born; he later described Peyronie's disease in 1743 and helped establish surgical education in France.

01-15.t: Birth of Trauma Surgeon Lorenz Böhler
01-15.s: Austrian surgeon Lorenz Böhler was born; he pioneered modern trauma care and defined Böhler's angle for evaluating calcaneal fractures.

01-16.s: Radiologists Charles T. Dotter and Melvin Judkins performed the first intentional percutaneous transluminal angioplasty on an 82-year-old patient's femoral artery, launching interventional radiology.

01-17.t: Birth of Anatomist Antonio Maria Valsalva
01-17.s: Italian anatomist Antonio Maria Valsalva was born; his studies of the ear and cardiovascular physiology led to the eponymous Valsalva maneuver.

01-17.t: Nazi Eighth Decree Bars Jewish Dentists, Veterinarians, and Pharmacists
01-17.s: Germany issued the Eighth Decree on the Reich Citizenship Law, revoking the licenses of Jewish dentists, veterinarians, and pharmacists and setting an expiration date for Jewish physicians.

01-18.s: The CDC and microbiologist Joseph McDade announced the isolation of the bacterium later named Legionella pneumophila, identifying the cause of the 1976 Philadelphia Legionnaires' disease outbreak.

01-18.t: First Use of the Zavanelli Maneuver for Shoulder Dystocia
01-18.s: Obstetrician William Zavanelli performed a novel cephalic replacement and cesarean delivery to resolve an intractable shoulder dystocia, now known as the Zavanelli maneuver.

01-19.t: Sir James Young Simpson First Uses Ether in Labor
01-19.s: Scottish obstetrician Sir James Young Simpson administered ether anesthesia during childbirth for the first time, before later introducing chloroform for obstetric analgesia.

01-20.t: Birth of Russian Neurologist Vladimir Bekhterev
01-20.s: Russian neurologist Vladimir Mikhailovich Bekhterev was born; he identified the role of the hippocampus in memory and described ankylosing spondylitis (Bekhterew disease).

01-20.t: CDC Confirms First U.S. Case of COVID-19
01-20.s: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed the first laboratory-proven case of SARS-CoV-2 in the United States in a patient in Snohomish County, Washington.

01-21.t: First Medical Treatise Printed in North America
01-21.s: Reverend Thomas Thacher published 'A brief rule to guide the common-people of New-England how to order themselves and theirs in the Small pocks, or Measels' in Boston.

01-21.t: Death of Nobel Laureate Camillo Golgi
01-21.s: Italian pathologist Camillo Golgi died; he shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Santiago Ramón y Cajal and discovered the Golgi apparatus.

01-22.s: Russian neuropsychiatrist Sergei Sergeievich Korsakoff was born; he later described the amnestic disorder associated with thiamine deficiency known as Korsakoff syndrome.

01-22.t: Dr. Roberta Bondar Becomes First Neurologist in Space
01-22.s: Canadian neurologist Roberta Bondar launched aboard Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-42) to study how microgravity affects motion sickness, balance, and cerebral blood flow.

01-23.t: Elizabeth Blackwell Earns First U.S. Medical Degree Awarded to a Woman
01-23.s: Elizabeth Blackwell graduated at the head of her class from Geneva Medical College in New York, becoming the first woman in the United States to receive a Doctor of Medicine degree.

01-23.t: First Successful Refined Insulin Treatment in a Human
01-23.s: At Toronto General Hospital, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson received a purified insulin injection prepared by James Collip, successfully reversing his diabetic ketoacidosis.

01-24.t: Birth of Otologist Heinrich Adolf Rinne
01-24.s: German otologist Heinrich Adolf Rinne was born; he developed the Rinne tuning-fork test to differentiate conductive from sensorineural hearing loss.

01-24.t: Death of Swiss Surgeon Fritz de Quervain
01-24.s: Swiss surgeon Fritz de Quervain died; he described both de Quervain tenosynovitis of the wrist and subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.

01-25.t: First Cesarean Section Under General Anesthesia
01-25.s: Surgeon Frederic Skey performed the first cesarean section under general ether anesthesia at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London, with the infant surviving the procedure.

01-26.t: Birth of Epidural Pioneer Fidel Pagés Miravé
01-26.s: Spanish military surgeon Fidel Pagés Miravé was born; in 1921 he published a landmark paper describing lumbar epidural anesthesia ('anestesia metamérica').

01-26.t: Dr. Janet G. Travell Appointed First Female Presidential Physician
01-26.s: U.S. President John F. Kennedy appointed myofascial pain specialist Dr. Janet G. Travell as his personal physician, making her the first woman in history to hold the role.

01-27.s: English physician Thomas Willis was born; he coined the term 'neurology' and described the arterial anastomotic ring at the base of the brain known as the Circle of Willis.
German neurologist Carl Friedrich Otto Westphal died; he described the deep tendon reflex sign (Westphal sign) and co-described the Edinger-Westphal nucleus.

01-28.t: First Reported Fatality Under Chloroform Anesthesia
01-28.s: Fifteen-year-old Hannah Greener died during a minor toenail procedure under chloroform anesthesia in England, prompting the first systematic investigations into anesthetic safety.

01-28.t: UK General Medical Council Rules Against Andrew Wakefield
01-28.s: The UK General Medical Council delivered disciplinary findings against Andrew Wakefield regarding ethical violations in his retracted 1998 Lancet paper linking the MMR vaccine to autism.

01-29.t: Destruction of the Anatomical Theatre of the Archiginnasio
01-29.s: During a World War II air raid on Bologna, Italy, the historic 17th-century Anatomical Theatre of the Archiginnasio was destroyed before later being reconstructed.

01-29.t: Birth of Nobel Laureate Linda B. Buck
01-29.s: American biologist Linda B. Buck was born; she shared the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Richard Axel for discovering odorant receptors and the organization of the olfactory system.

01-30.t: Death of Physician Robert Bentley Todd
01-30.s: Irish physician Robert Bentley Todd died; he described postictal Todd's palsy and pioneered the electrical theory of epilepsy in 1849.

01-30.t: Death of Anesthesia Pioneer Arthur Georg Läwen
01-30.s: German surgeon Arthur Georg Läwen died; he pioneered paravertebral nerve blocks, sacral anesthesia, and early clinical use of curare and artificial ventilation.

01-31.t: London Lock Hospital Opens First Venereal Disease Clinic
01-31.s: Founded by surgeon William Bromfeild, the London Lock Hospital opened at Grosvenor Place as the first voluntary hospital and clinic dedicated to treating venereal diseases.
